title: slop-diet Calibration Few-Shot Anchor Set
description: Blind human votes (pass/fail plus one-line note) on real Opus 5.5 outputs. Use them to calibrate the cold reviewer.
lessons: One sloppy detail fails the whole screen, even when the layout is strong.
Decorative colored dots were named in 3 of 9 notes. Treat any dot as a fail unless the brief asks for it.
Tinted pill tags next to dots read as sloppy.
An invented palette (cream page, black card, orange badge) reads as weird colors.
Too many effects at once fails ('trying too much'). Spend boldness in one place.
A hero visual that floats lower than the headline, or a half-empty chart, reads as off spacing.
An empty colored band above a heading fails.

anchors.evidence: .status::before { inline-size: 7px; block-size: 7px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor } in red, amber, blue and green per row.
Same table with icon-led severity badges. It passed narrowly; the dots were still the main complaint.

anchors.note: the color dots and pill, feels sloppy
anchors.evidence: 18px brown roast dots beside option names, six tinted .tag pills (Save 10%, For pour-over), cream page with clay accent.
Option cards with name and one line of text, selected card with green border, no dots, one count badge, order summary rail.
Cream page, black highlighted tier, orange button, orange badge and orange discount tag: three color roles fighting.
Dark hardware shell, one orange accent, live configurator with a running total rail.
Rack illustration, LEDs, multiple animated panels competing with the tiers.

anchors.note: the spacing is off, position of image
anchors.evidence: Chart card starts 60px below the headline top. Plotted data spans 20-160 Hz on a 20 Hz-20 kHz axis, so 60% of the chart is empty.

anchors.note: has block color room above heading
anchors.evidence: A tinted empty band sits above the hero heading.
